pr.title: Name inbox items by their text, not their number
pr.head: fcd028645d67292a2a2fff0c8e6384037c618131

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent post a question (with the ask tool) or a notice (with the tell tool) to a panel above the person's prompt. Each item gets a number in its session, such as 17. The agent uses that number to act on the item later, with the withdraw, revise, and restore tools, and it reads the number back in the ANSWER 17.a, DISMISSED 17, and RESTORED 17 messages that report what the person did.

The panel never draws that number. Agents still wrote "question 17" to the person, who had no way to tell which item that meant. This pull request leaves the panel alone and changes what agents read: every text that teaches an agent the inbox tools now says to name an item to the person by what it asks or tells.

• Tool descriptions. All five inbox tools end with one shared sentence, added in one place.
  • Tool results. The ask and tell results end with a sentence that says the same about the number they just returned.
  • Agent instructions. The Projector conventions block that project init writes into a repository's AGENTS.md says it, as version 14 of the block.
  • Documentation. docs/plugins.md and docs/cli.md each gain a sentence.
The numbers stay wherever a tool call or a project inbox command needs them.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, of c9b066f, found it clean and suggested one change: say that the panel never shows the number, rather than that the person never sees it, because project inbox list prints the number in a terminal.
  • fcd0286 makes that change everywhere the sentence appears and merges main. Its review found it clean, with no finding threads.

groups.title: What the inbox tools tell the agent
groups.kicker: The tool descriptions and results the agent reads during a session
intro: An agent learns the inbox tools from their descriptions, which hooks/inbox.ts defines, and it learns each item's number from the result of ask or tell, which hooks/register.tsx returns. Both now say that Projector's panel never shows the number, so the agent names the item to the person by its text.

The descriptions share one sentence, UNSEEN_NUMBER, which a small helper, described, appends to each description's own lines before joining them with spaces. Each description reads as before, with that sentence added at the end.

checks.text: claude plugin test . passes 144 of 144 at this head, including the new test that checks all five descriptions end with the shared sentence, and the panel tests that pin the full ask and tell results.

files.note: Adds the shared sentence and the described helper, and builds the five tool descriptions with it.
Ends the ask result with "name the question to them by what it asks" and the tell result with "name the notice to them by what it tells".

groups.title: What the generated agent instructions say
groups.kicker: Version 14 of the block that project init writes into AGENTS.md
intro: project init writes a Projector conventions block into a repository's AGENTS.md, between projector:begin and projector:end markers. The begin marker carries the block's version, so the CLI can tell when a repository's copy is behind the template. The template lives in src/projector/templates/agents-block.md.

This change edits the last sentence of the block's inbox paragraph: name an item to the tools by its number, and to the person by what it asks or tells. Because the text changed, the version moves from 13 to 14, and tests/test_instructions.py pins the new text's hash. This repository's own AGENTS.md, which its CLAUDE.md links to, carries the refreshed block.

checks.text: The block in AGENTS.md matches the template line for line, apart from the {projects_dir} placeholder the CLI fills in, and the Python suite, including test_the_template_text_is_pinned_to_its_version, passes at this head.

files.note: The template: the version moves to 14 and the inbox paragraph's last sentence splits the number's two audiences.
This repository's copy of the block, refreshed by project init.

groups.title: What the documentation tells people
groups.kicker: One sentence each in the plugin and CLI references
intro: docs/plugins.md describes the panel and the tools for the person using them. docs/cli.md describes the project inbox commands that the tools run. Each gains one sentence: the panel never shows the number, so an agent names an item to the person by its text. The rest of each changed paragraph is the same text, rewrapped.
